payload.feature:
Decision 0047 (docs/decisions/0047-the-finding-is-closed-by-name.md, accepted 2026-09-06, on main at 0b10649) is the whole commission: implement its six rulings and their enforcement bindings, and ship. Read the decision first and again before the result file; every claim below is restated from it and the decision outranks this text where they differ.

What it rules, in the order to build it:

1. `brokkr operator supersede` — a new operator verb beside retry and stop. It appends exactly one `operator/commanded` event to a TERMINAL run (status completed or stopped), with `command: "supersede"` and `args` of exactly `{ "findings": [<seq>, ...], "by": { "realm": <realm|null>, "run_id": <run>, "seq": <seq> }, "reason": <text> }`; `operator` and `command_id` as today. No `operator/accepted` follows — there is nothing to execute, and the fold refuses an acceptance on a terminal run by design. The CLI takes `--findings` (repeatable or comma-separated seqs), `--by-run`, `--by-seq`, optional `--by-realm`, and the existing `--reason`, and it opens the world the way the fleet verbs do (`--realms` default ./realms.json when present, `--db` outranking it), because `by` may live in another hearth. The write goes through the fenced append of decision 0029, and today's `brokkr operator retry|stop` behaviour is unchanged. Publish the args shape as `contracts/operator-supersede.v1.schema.json` — a payload schema over `args` for `command: "supersede"` and nothing else — and add its row to contracts/README.md under the additive rule (decision 0016's amendment); the v1 event envelope, the `type` enum and every witness digest do not move. Prove that in a test that folds a stopped run with a supersede annotation appended and asserts the folded state is byte-identical to the fold without it.

2. Cite or say nothing binds the operator. Before writing, the verb verifies and refuses, writing nothing, when: the annotated run is not terminal (on a running or parked run the fold would hold it as a pending command and `operator/accepted` would refuse it as unknown — say so in the refusal); any entry in `findings` is not the `seq` of a residual finding `brokkr_view::residual_findings` derives for that run today; `by.run_id` does not exist in the journal `by.realm` names (or the workspace journal when null), or `by.seq` is not a `transition/decided` event in it; or the superseding run is the annotated run. Each refusal path has a test. An annotation that verified at write time is not re-verified at read time; state that rule in the `residual_findings` docs and test it with a journal whose superseding run is later concluded and whose annotation still reads as written.

3. The fold does not read it; the view does. `fold` keeps treating the event as the no-op annotation it already admits after a terminal status (the `OperatorCommanded | OperatorRejected => Ok(())` arm in crates/brokkr-core/src/fold.rs); `RunState` gains nothing. `brokkr_view::ResidualFinding` gains one field, `superseded: null | { seq, by: { realm, run_id, seq }, reason, operator, recorded_at }`, where `seq` is the annotation's own sequence number on the annotated run; a finding named by more than one supersede carries the last in journal order. Every surface that prints a residual finding prints the mark — `inspect` and `tui` on the ruling line, `runs --json`, and the dossier. A view test plants an annotation and asserts the field; a replay test proves the fold is unchanged.

4. The dossier carries the mark, and the annotation is a citable fact. In `dossier_of` (crates/brokkr-cli/src/muninn.rs) each `residual_findings` entry carries `superseded` as ruling 3 states it; the annotation's `(realm, run_id, seq)` joins the dossier's closed set of facts so a report may cite it; the superseding run's `(realm, run_id, seq)` is stated as a fact when that run is in the world this reading covers; `counts` gains `superseded_findings`. Tests in muninn/tests.rs plant a superseded finding and assert the mark, the fact, and the count.

5. Muninn leaves a superseded finding out of the queue and says how many it left out. `agents/charters/muninn.md` gains one rule, in the charter's own plain register: a finding the dossier marks `superseded` is not queued; `fleet_summary` states in one clause how many findings were superseded and by what; a superseded finding whose superseding run is itself stopped or carries its own residual is still not queued — the superseding run's residuals are, on their own citation; Muninn may not propose a supersede, since `operator_commands` admits nothing on a terminal run and closing the record is the operator's alone. The `parked_runs` vocabulary does not widen. A Muninn test whose dossier carries a superseded finding asserts the citation check passes when the report cites the annotation and that the rendered queue omits the finding. Changing the charter moves the muninn agent's charter digest: re-pin whatever witness or library-data test carries it and say so in the commit.

6. The annotation is not a conclusion. It changes no status, no ruling, and grounds no rule in the phase machine. A run stopped on REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD stays stopped on it.

Also: `docs/guides/read-surfaces.md` gains the verb under the `brokkr muninn` section and the operator section, in the guides' voice; `brokkr operator --help` names the three commands. Do not annotate any real finding — this slice ships the verb and annotates nothing (the decision's consequences say so). Do not add a `reopen` verb or head-based staleness; the decision leaves both open.

Constraints: the exact coverage gate (scripts/coverage-exact.sh, run with stdin closed: </dev/null) must stay at literal 100%; clippy -D warnings and fmt must stay clean; cargo test --workspace green here and, by construction, on macOS and Windows (never compare a path against a string literal containing `/`); contracts/ existing files, fixtures/ and policy/phase-machine.json are read-only — the new schema and README row are additive; the decision index docs/decisions/README.md must keep every row main carries in number order, and 0047 stays accepted; do not name the private neighbours in prose; any list of agent CLIs in prose reads claude, codex or dsh; commit in the repository's style on top of 0b10649, citing decision 0047 by ruling number where code enforces it, and never push.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

result.notes: Framed decision 0047's six rulings in .forge/tasks/0047-supersede.md: new brokkr operator supersede verb (verify-then-single-fenced-append, no operator/accepted, distinct code path from today's retry|stop operator_command), operator-supersede.v1.schema.json as an additive args-payload extension, ResidualFinding.superseded field read by residual_findings (fold stays a no-op arm, unchanged), dossier_of + superseded_findings count in muninn.rs, a new muninn.md charter rule with its digest witness re-pinned, and doc/help updates. Called out concrete file locations (lib.rs Cmd::Operator ~301, engine.rs operator_command_racing ~2421-2538, view lib.rs ResidualFinding ~620/residual_findings ~667, muninn.rs dossier_of ~139-270), the read-surfaces.md ambiguity (no existing standalone operator section), and all house constraints (read-only contracts/fixtures/phase-machine, exact-coverage gate, clippy/fmt, no path-vs-string-literal comparisons, no backfill/reopen/head-staleness). No production code changed by this seat.

inputs.charter_digest_repin: none needed — agents/charters/muninn.md moved bytes but no witness or library-data test pins its sha256; muninn's charter enters no bundle manifest

gates.coverage_exact: lines 19928/19928, branches 3156/3156, no uncovered source function outside test harnesses; computed with the gate's own cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --locked --branch run and its LCOV arithmetic, because scripts/coverage-exact.sh itself is not runnable from this seat's shell

result.notes: Implemented decision 0047 whole, on top of 0b10649, committed (signed) as 80f36b0 on fire/0047-supersede; never pushed. Ruling 1: new `brokkr operator supersede` verb — runtime `operator_supersede` appends exactly one operator/commanded with command "supersede" and args {findings, by{realm,run_id,seq}, reason} to a terminal run, through decision 0029's fenced append; no operator/accepted follows; retry|stop behaviour and flags unchanged; args published as contracts/operator-supersede.v1.schema.json with a contracts/README.md row (envelope, type enum and witness digests unmoved) and a fold test proving byte-identical state. Ruling 2: verify-then-write with five refusal paths (non-terminal run, no findings named, a seq that is not a residual finding, a by-run/by-seq that does not resolve, self-supersede), each tested, each writing nothing; the write-time-only verification rule is documented on residual_findings and tested by concluding the superseding run afterwards. Ruling 3: fold untouched; ResidualFinding.superseded plus Ruling.superseded; the mark prints on inspect's ruling line, the tui/console trail row, runs --json (run rows now carry residuals) and the dossier; VIEW_VERSION 8 to 9. Ruling 4: dossier carries the mark, admits the annotation and (when covered) the superseding ruling to the citable fact set, counts superseded_findings. Ruling 5: muninn charter rule 5 plus the fleet_summary clause, with tests for the citation and the omitted queue entry. Ruling 6: nothing touches the phase machine, rules or status. brokkr-runtime gained a brokkr-view dependency (the verb checks ruling 2's finding condition against the one derivation rather than deriving residuals twice) and ARCHITECTURE.md draws the edge. Docs: read-surfaces.md gains the verb under `brokkr muninn` and a new `brokkr operator` section; `brokkr operator --help` names all three commands. No real finding was annotated; no reopen verb, no head-based staleness, no backfill. One caveat worth the operator's eye: scripts/coverage-exact.sh could not be invoked from this seat's restricted shell, so the gate was reproduced step by step with its own commands and its own LCOV arithmetic (clean run: llvm-cov clean, then the same --workspace --all-features --locked --branch run, then the lcov report) and came out at literal 100% on lines, branches and source-defined functions, with no test-harness source in the report; re-run the script itself before merging if you want the script's own word for it.
